steps.text: In a small bowl, combine the flour, salt and ground black pepper. Coat the beef cubes with this mixture.
Melt the butter or margarine in a large skillet over medium high heat. Add the meat and brown well on all sides. Pour this into a 2 quart casserole dish.

Return the skillet to the heat and add the onion, carrots and garlic to it. Saute for 5 to 10 minutes, or until onion is tender. add the wine, bay leaf, parsley, thyme, and liquid from the mushrooms. Pour over meat.
Bake, covered, at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 2 1/2 hours. Remove cover, add canned onions and mushroom crowns, and bake for 30 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Beef Bourguignon II
raw_recipe.description: Stewing meat is browned and braised in red wine with carrots, garlic, onions, and herbs. Mushrooms and more onions are added for the last half hour of cooking.
raw_recipe.name: Beef Bourguignon II

review.reviewBody: Wonderful, Wonderful!!!! This was a great recipe! I have never made this type of dish before and it turned out great! I used a London broil as my meat; it was a very nice cut I might add! I did not use fresh parsley, all I had on had was dried, but it didn't matter, it was still great! I have put this in my personal cookbook! I just want to add to anyone who wants to try this, please remember this and make it a rule of thumb, my mother always told me, never cook with a wine that you wouldn't drink, because when the alcohol cooks off, all you have left is the flavor, so please, make sure you use a good wine. I recommend CK Mondavi Cabernet Sauvignon. It is a great wine and reasonably priced.

My first time making this recipe. We served it over mashed potatoes. My husband LOVED it and had three helpings. It was delicious. Changed up a few things due to other reviews and my taste. Used a little over one cup of pinot noir and one full cup of beef broth. we do not eat mushrooms so added fresh green beans instead. Have a ton left over to enjoy and will add this recipe to my top 10. Chris in NH

Wish I’d done what many said about using beef broth. Really lacked flavor and needed lots of salt and pepper afterwards. Also should’ve salted the beef more and more herbs can go in everything. Obviously used fresh mushrooms and onions as well. Why cans?
I followed this recipe exactly. It tasted great, BUT, I ran dry. Not sure what to add next time to make it more saucey.

With the exception of not having mushroom liquid, I followed the recipe to a tee. The taste was so delicious!! I checked it an hour early just to stir things around and all the juices evaporated! Thankfully, I checked in time and took them, they were cooked through. I made a side of mashed potatoes to lay under the Beef Bourguignon II I will be making again.
Great recipe. Easy to make. Wonderful flavor. I upgraded the meat to sirloin beef tip roast and I used fresh mushrooms instead of canned.
Great recipe - thanks so much. Made it for my wife for Mother's Day. Everyone loved it! I used tenderloin and cut the time to 1 hour. Added pearl onions. Very tasty!
Easy to make and tastes like an expensive entreee at a restaurant!

Wonderfully reduced and delicious beef bourguignon. I didn't have a bay leaf or any pearl onions. I added an extra onion, sliced, at the beginning instead. I also had double the mushrooms on hand, that that was good because they pretty much disappeared. I used Chianti, as I could trust the flavor and brand. Served over egg noodles. You may need to salt and pepper as desired. Great with a fresh, hot loaf of French bread & butter, and perhaps a green salad.
Except for adding a tablespoon of tomato paste, I followed the recipe. It tasted okay but was way overcooked and somewhat dry. I will not be making again.
I used a Black Betty Shiraz wine.

I only changed a few things with this recipe. I used sirloin instead of stew meat. I doubled the amount of carrots and flour.. I deglazed the pan after cooking the meat. I cooked it for 7 hours in a Crock Pot on low. After four hours, I added the canned onions and mushrooms. The wine I used was Sterling Pinot Noir. I served it over Carba Nada Pasta. It was outstanding!
